hints.text: Subtracting logs means DIVIDING inside: $\log A - \log B = \log\left(\frac{A}{B}\right)$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: $\log_2(16) - \log_2(2) = \log_2(8) = 3$. Same move — divide inside first, then ask the log question once.

explanation: The quotient rule: subtracting logs is dividing inside.

alternativeExplanations.title: Break 96 into friendly pieces
steps: Now subtract $\log_2(3)$ from both sides — it cancels out.

alternativeExplanations.title: Undo twins
steps: Logs turn multiplying into adding, and dividing into subtracting.
So a subtraction outside must be a division inside: $96 \div 3 = 32$.
Count doublings to $32$: $2, 4, 8, 16, 32$ — five of them.
